comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
You'll get no arguments from me on the wipe issue. But to the matter at hand: The world clock is, as I understand it, divided into two sections -- Years (15th Century, 16th, etc.) and Periods (1st, 2nd, etc.) This much is simple enough. Unfortunately, some clock periods can have more than one event assigned to them. For example, 15th Century 5th Period has these three possible HEs:

The Cape of Good Hope (unlocks Prester John theme for the Ong Khan armor/relic)
Arriving at the New World
French Invasion of Italy

Of course, this particular HE is one of 3 possible 16th Century period 3 HEs, and its activation leads to the opening of Shining Hill TH theme, without which we cannot discover the second (and more beautiful) version of El Dorado. Price Revolution was the second HE of this WC period, and the third HE is immaterial to the topic at hand.

So in order to unlock both of those missing TH themes on Maris, we need the world clock to first turn to the correct period, then hope it activates the TH-related HE we want from among the list of possible HEs associated with that period. We have no idea what factors affect the selection choice; could be random, could be player related, who knows but the developers.

In other words... short of direct GM intervention (perhaps at the advice of CAs on behalf of the UWO community as a special event to bolster player attendance/engagement), there is no way I know of to accurately and precisely trigger those HE occurrences, making it all a "luck-based mission" which can only be attempted every two months, and maybe not even then depending on the capricious whims of which direction the clock moves in.

Source: gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?WorldClock

I've suggested before that players unite in their time-voting with Alias in Frankfurt; I also submit that perhaps CAs could suggest to GMs holding an event that purposely triggers this World Clock event, perhaps to celebrate the recent release (we know they have some power here as witness the Azores race incident).
